stage119_revised_abstract.content: Integrating Small Language Model (SLM) components into software systems introduces dependability challenges, including non-deterministic semantic hallucination and unauthorized action proposals. In this paper, we evaluate an externally enforced Policy-and-Evidence Intermediate Contract architecture that wraps generative components with typed semantic contracts and deterministic verification boundaries without altering model weights. In a design-based confirmatory trial over a frozen frame of $M=82$ open-source software manifest clusters ($N=240$ cases, $n=60$ sampled clusters), independently implemented Python~3.14 and Rust~1.99 interpreters achieved $100.0\%$ ($480/480$) mutual state and fact-level conformance ($p = 0.000965$, bounding frame failures to $\le 2/82$ at $95\%$ confidence). In an eight-condition factorial evaluation ($N=1,920$ matched outcomes using Phi-3.5-mini), the SLM selector achieved $0/120$ exact match on authorized queries due to distractor over-selection, yet full proposal recall enabled a deterministic evidence guard to recover $100.0\%$ ($120/120$) complete displays under template rendering. Generative rendering incurred a $36.67\%$ ($44/120$) utility omission penalty without safety gain. Equivalent specialized contracts produced identical outcomes, confirming that safety guarantees stem from the deterministic policy boundary rather than representation syntax.
